## Proposition 10.87
**Statement:** To find the third apotome.

**Step 1.** Let r be the assigned rational straight line. By 10.50 construct a third binomial relative to r, and denote its greater and lesser terms by a and b. We choose this construction because its terms already satisfy the required conditions; subtraction instead of addition will produce the desired apotome. [10.50]

**Step 2.** As the terms of a binomial, a and b are rational straight lines commensurable in square only. Since their sum is a third binomial, neither a nor b is commensurable in length with r. Moreover, the square on a exceeds the square on b by the square on a straight line c commensurable in length with a. [10.36; D10.2.1; D10.2.3]

**Step 3.** Since a is greater than b, cut off from a a segment equal to b, and call the remainder x. Because a and b are rational and commensurable in square only, x is an apotome. Its whole is a and its annex is b. [1.3; 10.73]

**Step 4.** Neither the whole a nor the annex b is commensurable in length with the assigned rational straight line r, and the square on the whole exceeds the square on the annex by the square on c, which is commensurable in length with the whole. Therefore x is a third apotome. Thus the required third apotome has been found. [D10.3.3]

**USED:** 1.3, 10.36, 10.50, 10.73, D10.2.1, D10.2.3, D10.3.3

heath_proof_text: Let a rational straight line A be set out, let three numbers E, BC, CD be set out which have not to one another the ratio which a square number has to a square number, but let CB have to BD the ratio which a square number has to a square number. Let it be contrived that, as E is to BC, so is the square on A to the square on FG, and, as BC is to CD, so is the square on FG to the square on GH. [X. 6] Since then, as E is to BC, so is the square on A to the square on FG, therefore the square on A is commensurable with the square on FG. [X. 6] But the square on A is rational; therefore the square on FG is also rational; therefore FG is rational. And, since E has not to BC the ratio which a square number has to a square number, therefore neither has the square on A to the square on FG the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore A is incommensurable in length with FG. [X. 9] Again, since, as BC is to CD, so is the square on FG to the square on GH, therefore the square on FG is commensurable with the square on GH. [X. 6] But the square on FG is rational; therefore the square on GH is also rational; therefore GH is rational. And, since BC has not to CD the ratio which a square number has to a square number, therefore neither has the square on FG to the square on GH the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore FG is incommensurable in length with GH. [X. 9] And both are rational; therefore FG, GH are rational straight lines commensurable in square only; therefore FH is an apotome. [X. 73] I say next that it is also a third apotome. For since, as E is to BC, so is the square on A to the square on FG, and, as BC is to CD, so is the square on FG to the square on HG, therefore, ex aequali, as E is to CD, so is the square on A to the square on HG. [V. 22] But E has not to CD the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore neither has the square on A to the square on GH the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore A is incommensurable in length with GH. [X. 9] Therefore neither of the straight lines FG, GH is commensurable in length with the rational straight line A set out. Now let the square on K be that by which the square on FG is greater than the square on GH. Since then, as BC is to CD, so is the square on FG to the square on GH, therefore, convertendo, as BC is to BD, so is the square on FG to the square on K. [V. 19] But BC has to BD the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore the square on FG also has to the square on K the ratio which a square number has to a square number. Therefore FG is commensurable in length with K, [X. 9] and the square on FG is greater than the square on GH by the square on a straight line commensurable with FG. And neither of the straight lines FG, GH is commensurable in length with the rational straight line A set out; therefore FH is a third apotome. [X. Deff. III. 3] Therefore the third apotome FH has been found.
